scope: Four archived outcome-selected development case/engine pairs from two source games, three Leela Zero#57 and one KataGo b6c96 s175M. Two cases overlap the same original chain at different times, and the game6 case overlaps across engines. No population failure-rate or independent confirmation claim.
branch_choice: Recorded engine move from archived128-visit seed11 discovery; first independently certified safe alternative in the archived annotation list. Moves frozen before new continuations. The historical source-game move is different and is not used as the recorded-engine arm.
ply_count: Ply1 is the forced branch move; subsequent moves are generated by the case's engine for both colors. Each branch starts a fresh native process from the complete original empty-board SGF prefix, including passes. No capture witness is forced for the opponent.
search: Single search thread; resignation, pondering, root policy noise and chosen-move temperature disabled. Preserve archived settings: Leela seeded native symmetries/pass heuristics; Kata forced identity, no NN cache, kata-search then play. Native tree reuse within a branch retained, never across arms. Check128 final root visits at every generated move, retain new playouts and actual wall time. Same branch seed is a pairing convention; divergent states consume different RNG histories.
rules: Preserve each native engine's prior rules: LZ built-in positional superko/no suicide/area; Kata Chinese SIMPLE ko/no suicide/AREA, verified from kata-get-rules. Independent sgfmill replay checks simple ko/no suicide and LZ full-prefix positional repetition (passes exempt). Kata native legality mask additionally checks every move. Compare native board to replay after every continuation move. Engine rule/symmetry differences prevent pooled cross-engine interpretations.
primary_outcome: All original target stones uncaptured through ply64, tracked permanently through merges and reoccupation. Any original-stone capture before64 resolves failure0. Reaching64 with every original stone retained resolves1. Early termination or engine error before64 with all target stones still present is unresolved, never silently carried forward. Fraction retained, first loss ply and complete-target loss ply also recorded.
decision: Case-by-case paired effect (defense minus recorded) over eight fixed seeds. Retain unresolved binary outcomes as[0,1]; report worst/best mean difference bounds. A positive primary preservation advantage is supported within this selected seed cohort only when its worst-case paired mean difference exceeds0. Otherwise report no robust advantage or unresolved. No p-values, confidence interval over positions, pooled prevalence estimate or optional seed extension. Repeated seeds do not increase independent case count.
secondary: Ply128 strict retention and fraction bounds; capture timing; early-terminal board retention; legal two-pass termination; physical terminal-board area and native final_score agreement. Terminal board retention is physical occupancy, not adjudicated life. Report a terminal result only after two passes and exact native/independent physical area-score agreement under source komi; score disagreements remain unresolved. Horizon-truncated branches do not get invented winners. Materially worse terminal results prevent any favorable whole-game interpretation; even favorable self-play results are not perfect-play/forced-win claims.
errors: Retain every planned branch, including error records and valid prefixes. No automatic retry of error observations, no dropped seeds. Partial progress is saved after each verified move; interrupted uncompleted branch files require a fully documented fresh-process rerun under the same freeze, not continuation of a partially lost engine state.
integrity: Before outcomes freeze cases, full source prefixes, implementation, model/binary hashes, all settings, seeds and analysis. Original binaries/models must match milestone4. Independent NumPy replay (separate from sgfmill production transitions) verifies every prefix and continuation, original identity removals, all native board hashes, fixed budgets, SGF reimports, score calculations, and source/record hashes. Save raw native logs and GTP transcripts.
engineering_pilot: Excluded empty-board seed701, three128-visit searches per engine. Leela0.028–0.046s/search, Kata0.479–0.709s/search, native binary/model hashes match archived originals. No target-case continuation outcomes observed before freeze.
next_order: After this development gate, separately reserve new attack families, then select matched ordinary controls. Do not reuse these source games as reserved confirmation. Keep Loops Look Alive manuscript/native-engine validation separate.
runtime: Original go-concept-lab Python3.9.10/NumPy2.0.2/sgfmill1.1.1; external binary/model paths supplied in an uncommitted locations JSON. Hash identities, not machine paths, are public. No new Go worker adapter is installed by this audit.
